newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Work starts on Vietnam-Japan glass factory.
newsitem.headline: Work starts on Vietnam-Japan glass factory.

text.p: Nippon Sheet Glass Co Ltd, trading firm Tomen Corp and a Vietnamese partner have started work on a factory north of Hanoi which will produce float glass for buildings and cars, an official said on Saturday.
The Vietnam Glass and Ceramic Corp (Viglacera) official, who declined to be named, said construction was scheduled to be completed and production under way by March 1998.
Nippon Sheet Glass has a 55 percent stake in the $126 million joint venture, while Tomen has 15 percent and Viglacera 30 percent.
Using local supplies of sand and dolomite, the factory will have production capacity of 28 million sq metres (72.5 million square yards) by 2001.
The official said the plant would operate at 80-90 percent of its final capacity level during the first years of operation, exporting 40 percent of the output.

Another Japanese firm, Asahi Glass, is planning to build a sheet glass factory with Vietnamese partners in Song Be province, north of Ho Chi Minh City, which would start operations in 1998. A Japanese newspaper report said last month that upon approval from the Vietnamese government, Asahi Glass would invest $100 million in the joint venture.
